chose: Bound the Scope first load by what it can never outgrow: a page-wide reference site window (SITE_WINDOW) shared evenly across the latest chokepoint entries, bypass sites always carried, every other site past an entry's share counted as a tally by component, endpoint, class and test mark (sitesLeft) so the map's run-site weights, exempt counts and bypass lists stay exact; the Reliance list says how many of its sites the page carries and the live page loads the rest from /api/sites, a snapshot names query relies-on. The journal window keeps each practice's latest STRIP_WINDOW enactments (what its strips read) and the enactments amendments cite, not every enactment; the rest are counted and the Practices view says how many it holds
over: a byte budget enforced in windowState with sites carried in a compact form (grouped by file, lines as numbers): a constant factor, still growing with the codebase times the chokepoints, and a budget that cuts by bytes would drop whichever part came last
a per-chokepoint site cap: still grows with every chokepoint added
raising the 3 MB limit: moves the day it fails
because: the runs part grows with the codebase times the chokepoints only through reference sites (313 KB of 671 KB on main, 1478 sites); a window over the whole page makes their cost a constant, and counting what is left by the keys every derivation reads keeps the no-silent-skip rule and every derived count. Enactments are 433 KB of the 693 KB journal part (156 records, all kept because the window assumed they were few) and grow every enact; the strips read only the latest 12 per practice. What then grows is the spec, the lexicon and the practices: declarations a human reviews

steps.text: run the totality oracles being refuted in one batched run confirmed with run --each (run --invariant <name>... --each), and see each green batched and alone
steps.leaves: run record for the bullets, pass; per-test run record, pass

steps.text: stage the smallest break that changes the behavior the bullet claims, not the strings the detector reads; read the diff to confirm the edit touched only the lines you meant
refute <component>/<name> --broke "<what you changed>"; the detector fails on its own assertion, not by a hang, a kill, a timeout, or what an earlier test left behind
steps.leaves: run record for the bullet, refutation red

steps.text: restore the source byte for byte: from HEAD when the code under test is committed, and from a copy taken before the break when it is not
steps.leaves: the file matches its state before the break (git diff against HEAD, or cmp against the copy)

steps.text: run them again in one batched run confirmed with run --each, and see each green batched and alone
steps.leaves: run record for the bullets, pass; per-test run record, pass

steps.text: when the red did not come from the break, record a decision that this refutation does not count and refute again; the run store is append-only, so the correction is a later record

a substring detector passed an unconditional early return that kept every expected string (df-c40bb904, x-429ed176)
the red came from the selected test depending on what earlier tests appended, not from the break (d-c4be0b1a, df-9e673484)

a break that turns a test red when the via does not test the claim refutes nothing; record unable instead (u-2e6ee400)
